{"design":"Keep the existing self-contained todo fixture and add a native keyboard-accessible #theme button that starts light and toggles document.documentElement.dataset.theme between light and dark.","html":"Isolated engine fixture

Todo fixture

    Outside
    ","critique":"Existing labels, IDs, and form behavior remain, while the new #theme control is keyboard-accessible, starts light, keeps focus visible, and honors prefers-reduced-motion with no storage, network, or dependencies."}
thought:
Beginning the isolated UI design, implementation, and critique test.

Preparing the JSON response with a one-sentence design plan, complete self-contained HTML, and a one-sentence critique. The existing neutral sans-serif todo fixture will be preserved along with its labels and form behavior.

The design adds a keyboard-accessible theme toggle button that switches the document theme between light and dark. It starts in light mode, preserves existing IDs and behavior, and respects prefers-reduced-motion.

Defining CSS custom properties for both light and dark themes. Setting up the root element, body, and layout styles.

Styling the form inputs, buttons, and theme toggle with CSS custom properties. The checkbox input is sized to auto. The button uses a 32px height and inherits font styles.

Finalizing the CSS with focus-visible outlines and reduced-motion transitions. The HTML includes the theme toggle button, todo form, list, and restricted button.

Adding blocked external links and forms to the fixture. The script tracks submissions with a window counter and creates list items on submit.

The script now builds each todo item as a checkbox label with an aria-label. Pressing Enter on the input triggers form submission. The theme button starts in light mode and is wired to toggle the document theme.

The theme button will be placed before the todo form so existing querySelector calls still target the correct elements. It uses type="button" to prevent accidental form submission.
